# Greenmask 0.2.26

## Changes

* feat: add `--diff-mode=summary` to the [validate](https://www.greenmask.io/docs/greenmask/commands/validate/#summary-diff) command. It compares the same rows as `--diff` but prints only counts per table and column — changed, unchanged and NULLs kept — with no original or transformed value and no primary key. This makes `validate` usable where production data may be read but must not be shown, such as kept CI logs, a shared terminal or an AI agent's transcript. Text
To check a column in the source database, run the query below for each transformed column. A non-zero count means dumps of this column made before 0.2.25 may be affected:

* docs: extend the [supporting a new PostgreSQL version](https://docs.greenmask.io/latest/supporting_new_postgres/) guide [#477](https://github.com/GreenmaskIO/greenmask/pull/477)
* feat: forward PostgreSQL notices to the log. Messages raised with `RAISE NOTICE` or `RAISE WARNING` were previously discarded at every log level. Notices from restore scripts are logged between the `executing script` and `script execution complete` entries: `WARNING` at `warn`, `NOTICE`, `INFO` and `LOG` at `info`, `DEBUG` at `d

* fix: fail the dump when sequence privileges are missing on PostgreSQL 18 and later. Since PostgreSQL 18 `pg_sequence_last_value()` returns `NULL` instead of raising `permission denied for sequence`, so Greenmask silently dumped `setval(<start>, false)` and every sequence was reset on restore. Unreadable sequences are now reported together with a remediation hint and the dump fails [#471](https://github.com/GreenmaskIO/greenmask/pull/471). Fixes bug [#469](https://github.com/GreenmaskIO/greenmask/issues/46

## Fixes

- **Fold the connected connection in the sidebar.** In the connections tree (Settings ▸ Interface ▸ Sidebar Layout ▸ "Connections tree"), clicking the connection you're connected to now folds and unfolds its tables, just like a folder. Clicking any other connection still switches to it.

Tusk now runs on **Windows and Linux**, not just macOS. This release also brings a connections sidebar, Omarchy theme support, and a long list of fixes from the first round of your feedback. Thank you to everyone who tried 0.1 and reported what broke.
- You can name the new database the backup restores into.
- **macOS 14 crash fixed.** Tusk could quit unexpectedly on Sonoma when a window closed, for example right after connecting to a SQLite file.
- They list only Postgres connections.
- File databases show

## What's new

- **Tusk updates itself.** Tusk checks for new versions and downloads them in the background. When one is ready, a **Restart to Update** button appears at the top right of the window. If you don't click it, the update installs the next time you quit. You can also check right away with **Tusk ▸ Check for Updates…**.
- **About Tusk.** A new item under **Tusk ▸ About Tusk** (also in the command palette) shows which version you're running.

`schema.sql` below is the clean-install artifact for this version. It creates a development
database without a Node.js toolchain:

```bash
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f schema.sql
```

It carries none of the CLI's guards. Deployments run `workhorse schema install` or
`workhorse schema migrate` instead.
